open_task_policy: Accept independently verified alternative constructions, counterexamples, and unexpected results. Explicit additional-hypothesis results are legitimate contributions but must not be relabeled as completion of the original scope. A short proof using applicable standard theorems is fully acceptable. Honest incompleteness is distinct from an invalid proof.
required_evidence: Specify a U-small Hausdorff realization M(X,Y), including its underlying set and topology, for every allowed Hausdorff X and Y.
Prove the natural identification C(S,M(X,Y)) = Nat(h_S times h_X,h_Y) for every profinite S, not merely the singleton case.
Construct the evaluation natural transformation and prove that its displayed operation is a bijection for every Hausdorff parameter Z.
Verify naturality in parameters and continuous maps of X and Y and respect the fixed universe throughout.
critical_errors: Assume X or Y is already compactly generated, or silently add local compactness of X.
Use C(X,Y) with ordinary function evaluation as the complete underlying record set without identifying the maps detected by probes.
Claim ordinary compact-open evaluation is continuous for arbitrary Hausdorff X.
Identify ordinary products with compactly generated products without proof.
Use singleton probes to identify a point map and stop before proving a topology represents all parameterized maps.
Claim uniqueness up to ordinary homeomorphism among all Hausdorff realizations from probe equivalence alone.
Use probes or Stone-Cech constructions outside U without a valid size argument.
completion_policy: The realization k C_co(kX,kY), its natural probe identification, and the evaluation-induced all-parameter exponential law suffice. Any equivalent Hausdorff realization and valid proof is accepted. Standard Cartesian closedness and compact-generation theorems may shorten the proof if their hypotheses, products, and sizes are matched. The two boundary examples and uniqueness discussion are optional. Reconstructing kX alone or disproving unqualified full faithfulness of original spaces does not complete this mapping-space task.
